Article Title: Captain falls ill, IndiGo Doha-BLR flight safely diverts to Muscat
Article Text:
IndiGo flight 6E 1302, operating from Doha to Bengaluru on Sept 3, 2026 was diverted to Muscat due to an urgent requirement of medical attention for one of the operating crew members. The said crew member was attended to by medical team upon landing and is feeling better now.

NEW DELHI: An IndiGo flight operating from Doha to Bengaluru (6E 1302) was diverted to Muscat after the pilot-in-command (PIC) fell ill. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed in Muscat. The airline is sending another aircraft to Muscat to fly passengers to their destination. The PIC has received medical care and has recovered."IndiGo flight 6E 1302, operating from Doha to Bengaluru on Sept 3, 2026 was diverted to Muscat due to an urgent requirement of medical attention for one of the operating crew members. The said crew member was attended to by medical team upon landing and is feeling better now,” an IndiGo spokesperson said."An alternate aircraft along with a new set of crew has been arranged to continue the journey to Bengaluru. We regret the inconvenience caused to our customers and are making all efforts to minimise it, including offering refreshments and timely updates as they wait for the aircraft at Muscat. The safety of our customers, crew, and aircraft remains our top priority at IndiGo,” the spokesperson added.
Article Summary: IndiGo flight operating from Doha to Bengaluru (6E 1302) was diverted to Muscat after the pilot-in-command (PIC) fell ill. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed in Muscat. The PIC has received medical care and has recovered. An alternate aircraft along with a new set of crew has been arranged to continue the journey.

Article Title: Former bureaucrat Ashish Joshi questioned by Delhi Police for 9 hours
Article Text:
The matter came to light after Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit, Joshi's friend, posted about it on X

NEW DELHI: Former bureaucrat Ashish Joshi was questioned by the Delhi Police Special Cell and was allowed to leave after nine hours on Wednesday, PTI reported.According to sources, Joshi, a former controller of communications in the Department of Telecommunications, had only been called for questioning in connection with an old case. Details of the case were not immediately available.The ex-civil servant was brought to the Special Cell’s office in New Friends Colony around 10 am and released around 7 pm. He was questioned by a team of the Counter Intelligence unit, which recorded his statement."Just got back home. Delhi Special Cell dropped me home. Details later," he posted on X after returning home.In a subsequent post, Joshi claimed he was taken for interrogration under an assurance that it would take "very little time.""However, as the hours stretched on, my repeated requests to inform my wife of my whereabouts, the concerned Police Officials/Officer simply stated they were 'following instructions.' I was only permitted to make a call at 6:38 PM, leaving my family & friends in total panic the entire day," he said, adding that informing a person's family during interrogation or detention is a legal mandate and not an "optional courtesy.The matter came to light after Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit claimed earlier on Wednesday that two Delhi Police personnel had “taken away” Joshi, whom he described as his close friend, from Nehru Park during his morning walk and that his whereabouts were unknown for several hours.According to Dikshit, Joshi, who retired as an additional secretary a few months ago, called him in the morning but he could not answer. When he tried calling back, the phone was switched off.“An eyewitness who was walking with him told the family that two police personnel came and said they had to take Ashish with them for questioning over a recent tweet,” the former MP claimed in a video statement.Dikshit also alleged that lawyers and others sent to the police station were initially unable to get confirmation about Joshi’s whereabouts.A senior police officer, requesting anonymity, maintained that Joshi and his family were duly informed about the case when he was brought in for questioning. He was questioned in a cordial manner and allowed to leave later, the officer added.
Article Summary: Ashish Joshi, a former controller of communications in the Department of Telecommunications, had only been called for questioning in connection with an old case. The matter came to light after Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit, Joshi's friend, posted about it on X. Joshi claimed he was taken for interrogration under an assurance that it would take "very little time"

Article Title: '23 Silkyara 'rat miners' offer to join Nepal tunnel rescue
Article Text:
A Delhi-NCR team of "rat miners" has offered to join rescue operations in Nepal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A Delhi-NCR team of "rat miners", whose manual excavation helped rescue all 41 workers trapped in Silkyara tunnel in 2023, has offered to join rescue operations in flood-hit Nepal, where at least 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects and about 500 are believed to be inside tunnels. Nepal Army has been prioritising search and rescue operations in 19 hydropower tunnels.Anand Kansal, Pune-based volunteer coordinator for the team, has written to Indian ambassador to Nepal, seeking help in placing the miners' expertise at the disposal of Nepalese authorities."We were highly moved after seeing news and videos (of the floods)... this is one of the worst tragedies we've witnessed in recent times," he said.Floods have damaged at least 12 hydropower projects in Rasuwa and Nuwakot - four under construction, seven operational and one undergoing testing - with mud, boulders and debris blocking or collapsing sections of tunnels.The miners came into national prominence during the Nov 2023 Silkyara-Bend-Barkot tunnel operation after mechanical drilling repeatedly failed. They entered a narrow rescue pipe and manually excavated the final stretch through the debris, helping rescuers reach 41 workers after 17 days underground.A 12-member team of the miners was also deployed at the Srisailam Left Bank Canal tunnel in Telangana in Feb 2025 after a collapse trapped eight workers. They worked there alongside specialised rescue agencies in difficult, debris-filled conditions.Firoz Qureshi, who took part in the Silkyara rescue, said the team was ready to leave immediately if Nepal sought its help. "We know what those families are going through right now, waiting for word. If we can go and help, we are ready today, not tomorrow."Monu Kumar, the youngest member of the group, said their manual techniques could be useful where heavy machinery was unable to penetrate. "Our hands and our tools can go where big machines cannot," he said. "We just need permission to go and start."
Article Summary: A Delhi-NCR team of "rat miners" has offered to join rescue operations in Nepal. At least 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects and about 500 are believed to be inside tunnels. Nepal Army has been prioritising search and rescue operations.

NEW DELHI: A dilapidated government school building in Rajasthan’s Rampura (Kanwarpura) village, whose poor condition was highlighted by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) last month, was demolished by authorities on Wednesday.Visuals from the spot show the old building being brought down by a bulldozer in the presence of officials from the district administration and education department.“A few days ago, our team was attacked while on their way to inspect this school, which was being run under a broken shed. The visit, however, led to a confrontation between CJP members and villagers, with FIRs being registered from both sides.

Article Title: Safai Karmachari Andolan counters govt reply in Parliament, claims manual scavenging still exists in atleast 46 districts
Article Text:
Muzaffar Ahmed Sheikh (35) from Ganderbal district in Jammu & Kashmir.

Mussi Devi (71) from Sitapur district in Uttar Pradesh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Challenging the Centre’s claim made in Parliament in the monsoon session that a survey conducted in all districts of the country during the year 2024-25 found no person engaged as a manual scavenger, Safai Karmachari Andolan (SKA) on Tuesday brought together women from Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and youth from Jammu & Kashmir claiming to be engaged in manual cleaning of human excreta in insanitary latrines to highlight that the illegal practice still persists in atleast 46 districts of these four states.National Convenor and co-founder of SKA, Bezwada Wilson said that they have evidence by way of photographs showing women lifting waste from dry latrines in these districts. “We will be writing to the ministry of social justice and empowerment to seek a fresh survey citing this evidence and demand action to stop the illegal practice in these districts within 60 days,” Wilson said.He, however, made it clear that if the ministry fails to act over the next two months, SKA teams will carry out a survey and put together a report by early next year. “We will highlight the findings across states and share them with Parliamentarians and the Judiciary to seek enforcement,” Wilson said.Former Supreme Court Judges Justice Madan Lokur and Justice Sudhandhu Dhulia and former Patna High Court Judge Justice Anjana Prakash expressed solidarity with the women and men who came forward to share heartwrenching experiences of a life marked by exploitation and untouchability despite the law in place wherein manual scavenging is illegal and dry latrines are banned.At the meeting held at Press Club of India as SKA announced the launch of a year long campaign ‘INDIA @ 80’ to free the country from manual scavenging, the former judges announced full support. Elaborating on the struggle by those involved in manual scavenging to break free, Justice Lokur expressed concern over the practice persisting despite the protection guaranteed by the Constitution of India against untouchability which is abolished and forbidden.He also dwelled on the long and continuing struggle for justice by those affected and how they have repeatedly ended up approaching the judiciary that has resulted in various directions from the Supreme Court from time to time. Justice Lokur highlighted that what is most worrying is the denial by authorities that the problem exists and the approach towards addressing the issue shows that ending the problem of manual scavenging is not a priority of the govt.He asserted that the govt must give priority to remove dry latrines wherever they remain. This he said should be a key focus area under the Swachh Bharat Mission.Justice Dhulia expressed shock that manual scavenging and dry latrines still exist in more than 40 districts and said that everyone must feel shame that such a practice continues to exist in our society.Justice Anjana Prakash too expressed concern over the lack of required efforts to end manual scavenging.As the workers shared their lived experiences as manual scavengers, one heard 71 - year - old Mussi Devi from Sitapur district in UP tell how her entire life has passed cleaning dry latrines and even now she is called by families in her area to manually clean-up and dispose of the waste. “When are we going to get freedom from this untouchability?,” asked Mussi Devi and others in her position. Ageing and frail, Devi is also the caregiver for her husband who is paralysed.35 - year - old Muzzafar Ahmed Sheikh from Jammu and Kashmir shared that he is the third generation in his family engaged in manual scavenging in dry latrines. He shared that his community is subjected to untouchability and even their houses are located in a separate cluster. He hails from Wussan village of Ganderbal. A father of a six - year - old, he says, “I want to break free from this identity of being a manual scavenger and I don’t want my son to grow up to do this ever. ”Bezwada Wilson summed up the sentiment of all those seeking justice. “I started the fight when I was 16 and now I am 60. Many things have changed but manual scavenging in dry latrines still remains. We have to end this menace without fail,” he asserted.It is pertinent to point that in the monsoon session of Parliament that concluded in August, in response to a written question in Lok Sabha by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, the minister of state for social justice and empowerment Ramdas Athawale said that as per the "Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 (MS Act, 2013)", a fresh survey has been conducted in all districts of the country during the year 2024-25 in which no manual scavenger has been found. “All the districts of the country have completed the survey and declared themselves as manual scavengers' free,” he said.However, he also added that 58,098 Manual Scavengers (MS) have been identified during two earlier surveys conducted in 2013 and 2018.Clearly differentiating "manual scavenging" and "hazardous cleaning", the minister shared while the later pertains to manual cleaning of a sewer or septic tank, without the employer providing protective gear, cleaning devices and safety precautions, a manual scavenger is defined as someone employed for manually cleaning, carrying, disposing of human excreta in an insanitary latrine.
Article Summary: Safai Karmachari Andolan (SKA) brought together women from Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Jammu & Kashmir claiming to be engaged in manual cleaning of human excreta in insanitary latrines. The illegal practice still persists in atleast 46 districts of these four states. SKA announced the launch of a year long campaign ‘INDIA @ 80’ to free the country from manual scavenging.

Article Title: Alphonso Smith Jr. cause of death: How did the former Broncos cornerback die at 40?
Article Text:
Alphonso Smith Jr. cause of death(Getty)

Alphonso Smith Jr. cause of death : Reports say he died by suicide in Florida

Alphonso Smith Jr. made his name with Wake Forest before reaching the NFL

Former NFL cornerback Alphonso Smith Jr. died at 40 in Florida on Wednesday, September 2, 2026. News of his death came after the former Denver Broncos and Detroit Lions player shared a disturbing Facebook message about his personal struggles. His final words quickly drew attention as fans looked back at the career of a defensive back who once stood out at both Wake Forest and in the NFL.According to reports, Smith died by suicide in Florida. His final Facebook post added a painful layer to the news. He wrote about fighting personal demons, apologized to people he believed he had hurt and said he had needed help.According to various reports, Smith died by suicide at a housing community in Florida. The reports cited sources with direct knowledge of the situation. Smith was 40. His death came shortly after he posted a lengthy message on Facebook. The former cornerback opened up about serious personal struggles and described trying to fight what he called “demons.” He also spoke about painful experiences from his childhood and reflected on how those experiences had affected him.“Do not cry for me! I tried everything in my power to fight the demons behind the ones that someone put into ME!” Smith wrote in his final Facebook post.The message became even more concerning as Smith continued. He apologized to his children, family, friends and others he believed he had hurt. He also indicated that he had tried to get help.“I did not want to be that WAY! I know I have disappointed so many folks. This is a DEMON in me! But not only me! It’s EVERYONE! I have HURT so many! I needed help & did not get it,” Smith wrote on Facebook.He ended the post with another apology and the words, “I am SORRY! THIS IS IT!”The message has since become a major part of the coverage surrounding his death. Still, the circumstances of his final moments remain private, and reports have offered only limited details about what happened in Florida.Smith’s football story started at Wake Forest, where he developed into one of the ACC’s top defensive backs. He finished his college career with 21 interceptions, a Wake Forest record and an ACC mark at the time.The Denver Broncos selected Smith No. 37 overall in the second round of the 2009 NFL Draft. He played 15 games during his rookie season before Denver traded him to the Detroit Lions in September 2010.The move gave Smith his best NFL opportunity. In 2010, he started 10 games for Detroit and recorded a team-high five interceptions. He also returned one interception for a touchdown and finished the season with 39 tackles.Smith remained with the Lions through the 2012 season. Across four NFL seasons from 2009 through 2012, he played 42 games and finished with 88 tackles and eight interceptions.His NFL career ended in 2012, but his accomplishments at Wake Forest and his time with Denver and Detroit remain part of his football legacy. Now, following his death on September 2, 2026, Smith is being remembered for far more than his years on the field.
Article Summary: Alphonso Smith Jr. died at 40 in Florida on Wednesday, September 2, 2026. Reports say he died by suicide at a housing community in Florida. His death came shortly after he posted a lengthy message on Facebook. He wrote about fighting personal demons, apologized to people he believed he had hurt.

Article Title: Argentina can't retire Messi's legendary No.10 because of the same FIFA rule that stopped them honouring Maradona in 2002
Article Text:
Argentina cannot retire Messi’s iconic No.10 because FIFA requires every World Cup squad number from 1 to 26 to be assigned/ Image: file

Argentina wanted to retire Maradona’s No.10 too

A pedestrian carries a bucket past graffiti depicting late soccer legend Diego Maradona in Buenos Aires, Argentina, Monday, April 13, 2026. (AP Photo/Rodrigo Abd)

Why FIFA will not let Argentina retire the shirt

Argentinian super fan Miloslav Urbanec shows his statue of Diego Maradona on a day of the World Cup semifinal match between Argentina and England, in the village of Bukovka, Czech Republic, Wednesday, July 15, 2026. (AP Photo/Petr David Josek)

Must read:

Messi’s No.10 has become impossible to separate from his legacy

Sport

Must read:

The next No.10 will inherit a shirt unlike any other

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lionel Messi’s retirement from international football has left Argentina with a question that feels almost impossible to answer: what happens to the No.10 shirt now? For many supporters, the obvious answer is to retire it forever. Messi wore it for two decades, became Argentina’s most-capped player and all-time leading scorer, and turned the shirt into one of the most recognisable symbols in world football. But Argentina has tried to do this before, when Diego Maradona was the player being honoured, and FIFA stopped it. More than two decades later, the same regulation stands in the way of giving Messi the ultimate tribute.The idea of retiring Argentina’s No.10 is not new, and its strongest precedent comes from the country’s other footballing icon.On 25 September 2001, the Argentine Football Association voted unanimously, on the initiative of then-president Julio Grondona, to retire the No.10 shirt in honour of Maradona.The plan was to put the decision into effect before the 2002 World Cup, and at the time it appeared to be settled. Argentine newspaper Olé even ran a front-page headline declaring: "It is God's will."There was, however, one problem: FIFA had its own rules governing squad numbers at its tournaments.FIFA rejected Argentina’s request, meaning the No.10 could not simply disappear from the World Cup squad. Ariel "El Burrito" Ortega ultimately wore the shirt for Argentina at the 2002 tournament, becoming the player who wore the famous number most prominently between the Maradona and Messi eras.The significance of that episode has returned now that Messi has stepped away from the national team.This time, it is not Maradona’s name attached to the request. It is Messi’s.The obstacle is not a lack of willingness from Argentina. It is the numbering system FIFA applies to its official tournaments.According to Marca, FIFA regulations require tournament squad lists for competitions such as the World Cup and Copa America to use consecutive numbers from 1 to 26. Every player selected for the 26-man squad must therefore have a number, with none omitted.That makes retiring the No.10 impossible in an official tournament.Argentina could want to leave the number untouched, supporters could overwhelmingly back the idea and the Argentine Football Association could decide that nobody should wear it again, but the regulations would still require the No.10 to be assigned to somebody when the team enters a tournament governed by FIFA's squad-number rules.In other words, Argentina cannot simply submit a 26-man squad numbered 1 through 9 and 11 through 27, or leave the No.10 blank as a permanent tribute to Messi. The numbering requirement creates a direct conflict with the idea of permanently retiring the shirt.That is exactly what happened with Maradona.The regulation therefore means Messi's No.10 can be treated differently in friendly matches, where Argentina could choose not to use the number, but the situation changes as soon as the national team enters an official tournament.The desire to retire the shirt is understandable because Messi did far more than simply inherit Maradona's number.He wore No.10 for Argentina for roughly two decades and leaves the national team as its all-time leading scorer and most-capped player. His international career also transformed the meaning of the shirt for another generation of Argentine supporters, just as Maradona had done before him.That is why the debate is not really about who deserves to wear the number next. It is about whether anybody should wear it at all.The Argentine Football Association has previously expressed a clear desire to retire the shirt once Messi ended his international career.In 2024, AFA president Claudio Tapia told: "The national team's number 10 shirt will be retired when Messi ends his international career."Tapia's comments made the association's intention clear, but the practical problem was always going to be FIFA's tournament regulations.The situation leaves Argentina with an unusual compromise. The No.10 could effectively be reserved as Messi's number whenever the team plays certain friendlies, allowing the association and supporters to honour him without giving the shirt to another player.But when the next World Cup or Copa America arrives, the number cannot simply be erased from Argentina's squad list.Someone will have to wear it.That leaves Argentina facing another difficult question: if the No.10 cannot be retired, who takes it?Messi's successor will inevitably inherit a shirt carrying the weight of both him and Maradona. It is one thing to wear the No.10 for Argentina; it is another to wear the number that has belonged to two of the country's greatest footballers.Several names could enter the conversation, including Alexis Mac Allister, Enzo Fernández, Thiago Almada and Nico Paz.According to ESPN Argentina insider Federico Bueno, Argentina have an internal plan for Paz to take the No.10 if Lionel Scaloni renews his contract as head coach, with negotiations expected to take place in the coming months.For now, though, the immediate reality is simpler: Messi's No.10 cannot be permanently removed from Argentina's official tournament squad.Maradona's Argentina tried it in 2001 and FIFA said no. More than 20 years later, the same rule means Messi's shirt faces the same fate.
Article Summary: Lionel Messi’s retirement from international football has left Argentina with a question that feels almost impossible to answer. For many supporters, the obvious answer is to retire it forever. Argentina has tried to do this before, when Diego Maradona was the player being honoured, and FIFA stopped it. FIFA regulations require tournament squad lists for competitions such as the World Cup and Copa America to use consecutive numbers from 1 to 26.

Article Title: Naomi Osaka reveals “long bouts of depression” as tennis superstar makes powerful stand for her wellbeing
Article Text:
Naomi Osaka (Getty Images)

Naomi Osaka and the French Open controversy

Naomi Osaka’s mental health message drew support

In May 2021, Naomi Osaka made a decision that shook the tennis world. The four-time Grand Slam champion withdrew from the French Open after refusing post-match media conferences, saying she was protecting her mental health. What followed was a wider debate about athletes, media duties and the pressure that comes with competing under a global spotlight.The controversy began before Osaka even played her opening match at Roland Garros. The Japanese star announced that she would not attend news conferences during the tournament because of the anxiety she experienced around speaking to the media.After beating Romania’s Patricia Maria Tig in straight sets, Osaka was fined $15,000 for skipping her post-match media duties. The situation escalated when the four Grand Slam organisers warned that continued refusal could result in heavier fines and possible suspension.Osaka then chose to leave the tournament.Her decision was not simply about avoiding questions after matches. In her statement, she explained the personal struggle behind it."The truth is I have suffered long bouts of depression since the US Open in 2018 and I have had a really hard time coping with that."She also described how social anxiety affected her around tournaments."Anyone that knows me knows I am introverted and anyone that has seen me at tournaments will notice that I'm often wearing headphones as that helps dull my social anxiety."Those words changed the tone of the conversation. What had initially looked like a dispute over media obligations became a much larger discussion about the emotional demands placed on elite athletes.Osaka acknowledged that her timing could have been better, but she stood by her decision to put her wellbeing first.I never wanted to be a distraction and I accept my timing was not ideal and my message could have been clearer. More importantly, I would never trivialise mental health or use the term lightly."The truth is I have suffered long bouts of depression since the US Open in 2018 and I have had a really hard time coping with that."Anyone that knows me knows I am introverted and anyone that has seen me at tournaments will notice that I'm often wearing headphones as that helps dull my social anxiety."Though the tennis press has always been kind to me (and I want to apologise to all the cool journalists who I may have hurt), I am not a natural public speaker and get huge waves of anxiety before I speak to the world's media."I get really nervous and find it stressful to always try to engage and give you the best answers I can."So here in Paris I was already feeling vulnerable and anxious, so I thought it was better to exercise self-care and skip the press conferences. I announced it preemptively because I do feel like the rules are quite outdated in parts and I wanted to highlight that."I wrote privately to the tournament apologising and saying that I would be more than happy to speak with them after the tournament as the Slams are intense."I'm going to take some time away from the court now, but when the time is right I really want to work with the Tour to discuss ways we can make things better for the players, press and fans."
Article Summary: Naomi Osaka withdrew from the French Open after refusing post-match media conferences. The four-time Grand Slam champion said she was protecting her mental health. Her decision sparked a wider debate about athletes, media duties and the pressure that comes with competing under a global spotlight.

Naomi Osaka opened her US Open campaign with an outfit built entirely around one man, and it is Allen Iverson. The four-time Grand Slam champion walked onto Arthur Ashe Stadium wearing his signature headband and arm sleeve, tucked under a gray hooded robe covered in newspaper clippings from her own career, paired with a wide, floor-length skirt.She won the match in straight sets, but the outfit had people talking before a ball was even struck. By Monday night, Iverson had noticed too, and he had something to say about it.Naomi Osaka beat unseeded Russian Anastasia Zakharova 7-6, 7-6 in her opening match, but the real story arrived before the first serve. Her robe, worn as she entered Ashe, was stitched with burnout newspaper clippings tracing her own career, a nod to Iverson's habit of turning up in whatever he wanted rather than what the league expected. She kept it simple when asked why. "It's my tribute to Iverson. I really like him a lot," she said afterward.The look was part of a broader Nike push linking tennis to basketball at this year's tournament. Aryna Sabalenka wore a mesh jersey in an orange shade tied to the Knicks for her own first-round win earlier that day.Osaka had already signaled where her loyalty sat days before, wearing a shirt printed with an old SLAM magazine cover of Iverson and calling him someone who reshaped how NBA players dress, on and off the court.Osaka admitted she had never actually met Iverson, only that she hoped he would see the outfit. And he did. The Hall of Famer posted his reaction on Instagram within hours: "Wow, what a honor!! BIG FAN can't wait to meet you."Designers Téla D'Amore and Ev Bravado, who built the piece, said Osaka and stylist Law Roach sent them two reference photos of Iverson in his headband, then gave them roughly 30 hours to construct the rest around that image.The result carried Iverson's off-court signature almost exactly: the sweats, the sleeve, the headband worn low.This is far from Osaka's first fashion statement of the year. At the Australian Open, she arrived under a wide-brimmed veil and parasol in a jellyfish-inspired look. At the French Open, she unveiled a black corset made from her own old Nike gear before switching into a gold dress she compared to the Eiffel Tower at night. At Wimbledon, she worked within the tournament's all-white rule to build a kimono-inspired outfit honoring Japanese design traditions.Osaka finished Monday's win with 11 aces against three double faults, despite 30 unforced errors along the way. She now moves on to face Kateřina Siniaková in the second round on Wednesday.

Article Title: Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family
Article Text:
Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family

What did Andre Agassi mean when he said, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood”?

What does Agassi’s quote tell us about his idea of parenthood?

Andre Agassi’s words, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” offer a deeply personal look at how becoming a parent changed the tennis legend’s view of his own life. Agassi grew up in a world where tennis was not simply a sport but a major part of his everyday life, with intense training and expectations starting at a very young age. Years later, after becoming one of tennis’ biggest stars, he and his wife, fellow tennis legend Steffi Graf, built a family life around their two children, Jaden and Jaz. For Agassi, watching his children grow gave him the chance to experience some of the simple moments of childhood that he felt he had missed himself.The quote is closely connected to Agassi’s own experience growing up. He started playing tennis as a young child and was pushed toward the sport by his father, Mike Agassi. His father had a clear dream for him: he wanted his son to become one of the best tennis players in the world.That dream eventually came true.Agassi went on to become world No. 1 and won eight Grand Slam singles titles during his career. But reaching that level meant spending much of his childhood training, competing and preparing for professional tennis.For a young child, that kind of life can leave little room for ordinary experiences. Instead of having complete freedom to decide how he wanted to spend his time, Agassi’s days were largely connected to tennis.That is where his famous quote becomes especially powerful.When he says he “gave up” his childhood, he is looking back at the years he spent becoming a professional athlete. But he is also talking about what those sacrifices eventually allowed him to do.His success gave him the freedom to step away from tennis and spend more time with his family. It allowed him to be present as his children grew up.In other words, Agassi may have missed parts of his own childhood, but later he had the opportunity to sit beside his children and watch them experience theirs. For him, that became a kind of second chance.Fatherhood gave Andre Agassi a different way of looking at his past. When he watched Jaden and Jaz grow up, he could see the small moments of childhood from a parent’s point of view.He could watch them discover what they liked, make their own choices and develop personalities separate from their famous parents.Those moments were very different from the childhood Agassi had experienced.His early years were strongly connected to the tennis court. His father believed that constant practice and discipline were necessary if Andre Agassi was going to become a champion. That approach helped produce an incredible tennis career, but it also meant that Agassi’s childhood was far from ordinary.As a father, he wanted something different for his children.Instead of seeing childhood as preparation for a future career, Agassi wanted Jaden and Jaz to enjoy the years they were living through.That is one of the most important ideas behind his quote. He was not simply saying that he wanted to give his children more material things or better opportunities. He wanted to give them time.Time to grow.Time to explore.Time to make mistakes.Time to decide what they wanted for themselves.This became especially important because Agassi knew from personal experience how powerful parental expectations can be. He had spent years trying to become the player his father wanted him to be. As a parent, he had the chance to make sure his own children did not feel that same pressure.Steffi Graf’s role in the family’s story is important because she understood Agassi’s world better than almost anyone. Like her husband, Graf was introduced to tennis at a very young age and went on to become one of the greatest players in the history of the sport.Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles and spent years at the top of women’s tennis before retiring in 1999. Agassi and Graf later married and raised their two children, Jaden and Jaz.Together, they had something unusual in common: both parents knew exactly what it took to become a tennis champion, but they also knew the pressure that came with that journey.That understanding appears to have influenced the way they raised their children.Despite having two parents who were global tennis stars, Jaden and Jaz were not simply expected to follow the same path.Jaden developed a passion for baseball rather than choosing tennis as his main sport. Jaz has also been able to follow her own interests. Andre Agassi and Graf have supported their children without making their parents’ careers the center of their lives.That is particularly meaningful when viewed alongside Agassi’s quote.The couple had already achieved what many athletes spend their entire lives chasing. They did not need their children to continue that legacy for them.Instead, they could give their children something that both parents understood the value of: choice.Agassi has also spoken warmly about Graf and the role she plays in his life. Their shared experience in professional sports gave them an understanding of the demands and sacrifices that come with elite competition.For their family, giving their children the freedom to choose their own paths became more important than creating another generation of tennis champions.At its heart, Agassi’s quote is about turning his own difficult experiences into something positive for his children.He cannot go back and change the childhood he had. He cannot erase the years of training, pressure and expectations that came with becoming a tennis player.But he can choose what kind of childhood his own children experience.That is what makes the quote about much more than tennis.Many parents work hard because they want their children to have opportunities they did not have themselves. Agassi’s story takes that idea one step further. His goal was not simply to provide his children with a comfortable life. He wanted to be present for the experiences that make childhood special.His words also show that parenthood can change the way people understand their own past.The same childhood that once felt difficult to Agassi became part of what helped him understand his children better. His experiences taught him what pressure can feel like, which may have made him more aware of the importance of giving his own children freedom.And Steffi Graf was there beside him, bringing her own experience as a former champion and a parent.Together, Agassi and Graf chose not to make their children’s lives about living up to their parents’ names. They allowed Jaden and Jaz to build identities of their own.That may be the most powerful part of Agassi’s words.He spent his childhood becoming a tennis champion. But when he became a father, he did not want his children to spend their childhood becoming something for him.He wanted to watch them simply be children.So, when Agassi says, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” he is not only talking about sacrifice. He is talking about perspective, presence and love.He gave years of his life to tennis. Those years helped him become a champion and eventually gave him the freedom to step back and focus on his family.For Agassi, one of the greatest rewards was not another trophy or achievement. It was being able to watch his children grow up on their own terms, with Graf by his side.That is what makes his quote so relatable. Parenthood does not allow us to rewrite our own childhoods, but it can give us the chance to create a different childhood for the next generation.
Article Summary: Tennis legend Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf have two children, Jaden and Jaz. Agassi’s famous quote, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children's childhood,” offers a look at how becoming a parent changed his view of his own life. For Agassi, watching his children grow gave him the chance to experience some of the simple moments of childhood.

Article Title: Ram Temple Trust inducts 3 new trustees, elevates Govind Giri as general secretary
Article Text:
The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has inducted three new trustees

Newly Inducted Member Mahesh Bhagchandka To Take Over As Treasurer





LUCKNOW/AYODHYA: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust on Wednesday inducted three new trustees and carried out a key reshuffle of its office-bearers, elevating Swami Govind Dev Giri as general secretary and appointing Delhi-based businessman and philanthropist Mahesh Bhagchandka as treasurer. Bhagchandka is one of the three newly inducted members of the trust.The appointments, approved at the Trust’s meeting in Ayodhya , fill all vacant positions in the governing body and mark a significant organisational transition as the Trust moves towards a more structured administrative framework with the selection of its first chief executive officer on .The new trustees, apart from Bhagchandka, are advocate Madan Mohan Pandey and educationist Dr Nirmala Yadav, bringing experience in philanthropy, law, education and public life to the board.Govind Dev Giri, who had been serving as treasurer since the trust’s formation in 2020, has been elevated to the position of general secretary following the exit of Champat Rai from the Trust’s executive structure. Dr Krishna Mohan, who had been functioning as interim general secretary since July 6, will continue as a trustee.Officials associated with the Trust described the developments as an important step towards strengthening the institution’s governance as the Ram temple complex expands its administrative, religious and pilgrim-management responsibilities.Bhagchandka, 68, is founder-trustee of the Ashok Singhal Foundation and is closely associated with initiatives linked to the legacy of late VHP leader Ashok Singhal, one of the most prominent faces of the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. A Delhi-based businessman, Bhagchandka participated as a yajman during both the bhoomi pujan and pran pratishtha ceremonies of the Ram temple.His association with Ram-related cultural initiatives includes work connected with the Shri Ram Van Gaman Yatra and the installation of Ram Stambhs at 292 sacred sites associated with Lord Ram’s exile route. He is also a member of the executive committee of the World Hindu Economic Forum.Trust insiders believe Bhagchandka’s experience in managing diversified business interests and his long association with socio-religious organisations will be valuable as the temple management expands its institutional structure.A nephew of veteran VHP functionary Satyanarayana Bhagchandka, he has also authored Hindutva ke Purodha, a book documenting the contribution of key figures associated with the Hindutva movement, including Ashok Singhal.The second appointee, Madan Mohan Pandey, 74, is among the legal figures most closely associated with the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. The Ayodhya-based advocate represented Shri Ram Lalla Virajman and late Mahant Ramchandra Paramhans Das in the Ram Janmabhoomi title dispute from 1990 until the conclusion of the case before the Supreme Court in 2019.His association with the litigation places him among those directly involved in the legal journey that culminated in the landmark Supreme Court verdict paving the way for the construction of the Ram temple.Pandey has also served as Uttar Pradesh’s additional advocate general for six years and remains associated with several religious and educational institutions. He is vice-president of the Shri Hari Satsang Samiti and patron of the Kathakar Yojana training centre in Ayodhya.The third trustee, Dr Nirmala Yadav, brings an academic and administrative background to the Trust. A former principal of BDM Girls PG College, Shikohabad, and later Mahatma Gandhi Vidyalaya PG College, Firozabad, she retired in 2022 after a long career in higher education.Yadav comes from a family with deep roots in education and public life in western Uttar Pradesh. Her late husband, advocate Harendra Yadav, served as an RSS district chief, while her father-in-law, Squadron Leader Surya Kumar Yadav, served in the Indian Air Force and was later associated with the erstwhile Jana Sangh.According to family members, the association of the Yadav family with education dates back more than a century to the establishment of Kanhai College in Shikohabad by Chaudhary Shyam Singh Yadav in 1916. The family has also produced public representatives and military officers, including former MLA Captain Nihal Singh and Squadron Leader Surya Kumar Yadav.With the induction of the three trustees, the Trust now has its full complement of 11 permanent members. Along with president Mahant Nritya Gopal Das, the governing body comprises general secretary Swami Govind Dev Giri, treasurer Mahesh Bhagchandka, Swami Vasudevanand Saraswati, Swami Vishwaprasannatheertha, Yugpurush Paramanand Giri, Mahant Dinendra Das, K. Parasaran, Dr Krishna Mohan, Madan Mohan Pandey and Dr Nirmala Yadav. Four ex-officio members also continue to be associated with the Trust.The reconstituted board is expected to play a central role in streamlining the functioning of the temple complex and finalising the administrative framework for the newly created CEO position. Trust members are also likely to consult legal experts while defining the powers, reporting structure and responsibilities of the chief executive officer as the institution enters its next phase of growth.
Article Summary: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has inducted three new trustees. Swami Govind Dev Giri has been elevated to the position of general secretary. Delhi-based businessman and philanthropist Mahesh Bhagchandka is appointed treasurer.

Article Title: ABVP pulls off a rare repeat in Panjab University polls: Retains president post, 1st back-to-back win since 2014
Article Text:
Chandigarh, Aug 31 (ANI): Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and SOI (Student Organisation of India) members celebrate after ABVP candidate Ankit Bidhan won the Punjab University Student Council election, in Chandigarh on Monday. (ANI Video Grab)

Retains PUCSC Prez Post, First Back-to-Back Wins Since ’14





CHANDIGARH: After ending its 48-year wait for the PUCSC presidency last year, ABVP retained the post on Monday, becoming the first student organisation since NSUI's back-to-back victories in 2013 and 2014 to achieve consecutive wins. The margin between the two triumphs is strikingly small.ABVP's presidential tally rose by just one vote, from Gaurav Veer Sohal's 3,148 last year to Ankit Bidhan's 3,149 this year. Yet that solitary vote marks the difference between a historic breakthrough and an equally historic repeat.The total presidential vote was almost identical too. Last year, the eight candidates and NOTA together polled 9,613 votes; this year, the four candidates and NOTA accounted for 9,610. The size of the presidential vote pool barely changed- but its distribution did.In 2025, Sohal’s 3,148 votes were followed by Student Front’s Sumit Kumar at 2,660, NSUI’s Parabjot Singh Gill at 1,359 and ASAP’s Mankirat Mann at 1,184. This year, Ankit’s 3,149 was followed by ASAP’s Aadil Brar at 2,637, NSUI’s Gurman Singh Sidhu at 2,263 and SATH’s Darshpreet Singh at 1,387. NOTA fell from 188 to 174.The change in the field matters. Sohal had won 32.75 per cent of the presidential vote last year; Ankit’s share is almost identical at 32.8 per cent.Yet the winning margin increased from 488 to 512 votes. ABVP’s vote base has effectively remained unchanged while its lead has grown.That points to the opposition arithmetic. Last year, Sumit alone came within 488 votes of Sohal, while Gill and Mann together polled 2,543. This year, the opposition vote was still larger collectively, but it was divided among three challengers, with none matching Sumit’s 2,660.For ABVP, there was another significant change. Last year, the organisation itself was divided, with the ABVP Front contesting the vice-president’s post separately; its candidate Naveen Kumar polled 2,828. This year, the outfit went to the polls together.
Article Summary: ABVP becomes the first student organisation since NSUI's back-to-back victories in 2013 and 2014 to achieve consecutive wins. The margin between the two triumphs is strikingly small. ABVP's presidential tally rose by just one vote, from Gaurav Veer Sohal's 3,148 last year to Ankit Bidhan's 3,.149 this year.

Article Title: First exam reforms, now 'school thik karo' campaign: How CJP is changing the discourse of politics
Article Text:
School students protest in UP

'Ministers’ dogs got better facilities than students'

CJP claims credit

Political parties take a cue from CJP

Youth outreach

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the biggest issue facing government school students today? Lack of teachers Poor infrastructure Caste discrimination Inadequate facilities 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: From colleges to schools. From Gen Z to Gen Alpha. From Jantar Mantar to cities and villages in states. The students’ protest has continued; only the stage has shifted. The Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) “School Thik Karo” campaign has put the spotlight on the sorry condition of government schools in many states. Gen Z showed the way from Jantar Mantar when they forced the NDA government to make Dharmendra Pradhan resign over NEET paper leaks. Gen Alpha took the cue and brought the protests to villages and towns across states, demanding better school infrastructure and government accountability.The CJP campaign asking for school audits in villages got a huge response. The pictures and videos of schools uploaded on CJP’s X timeline exposed the sorry state of government schools across states. This was followed by ground inspections by CJP teams, which led to confrontation and a strong pushback by some state governments.Two days after the CJP launched its campaign and announced that schools in Rajasthan would be on its radar, the state education department issued new guidelines regulating the entry of outsiders, including media personnel, into government schools.Under the directives, photography, videography, interviews, audio recording and live streaming involving students or school activities on campus needed prior permission from the school principal or head of the institution.The Rajasthan order went on to threaten action under applicable laws in case of any breach.So, when a CJP team went to inspect a government school on August 21, it was attacked and forcibly pushed back, allegedly by the locals. Videos of the incident showed a large number of people engaging in a heated exchange with the CJP team, pushing and shoving its members as they tried to enter the village. Some clips also showed stone-pelting and smashed windows of cars. Locals said the village did not need outside political groups to intervene in the school’s affairs.This perhaps became the July 20 Jantar Mantar moment (when Delhi Police used force to stop Gen Z protesters from their Sansad march) of the CJP school campaign as the violent confrontation propelled the issue to the national centre stage.Meanwhile in Uttar Pradesh, Gen Alpha students of a government school staged a protest twice, in a span of four days. over shortage of subject teachers. They briefly blocked traffic also. Students of a government school in Kannauj boycotted classes and held protests against the principal for alleged caste discrimination and ordering the felling of trees inside the school campus. The students of PM Shri Composite School in Gugarapur surrounded the vehicle of the in-charge principal at the school gate as he was leaving and raised slogans against him.Protests also happened in Fatehpur, Hamirpur against lack of facilities in schools. In Hamirpur, 'Gen Alpha' children laid siege to the collectorate to demand the construction of a paved road to their school.In Unnao, hundreds of students of a government-run residential school staged a protest over alleged poor-quality food, inadequate drinking water, shortage of teachers and the behaviour of the principal, briefly disrupting traffic at a city crossing.In Maharashtra, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke conducted a social audit of government-run and municipal schools in Latur district. He led a team at a Zilla Parishad school at Ujani village in Latur's Ausa tehsil.After his audit, Dipke said schools in the state were in a pitiable condition, and even "ministers’ dogs got better facilities" than students. He sought the resignation of Maharashtra school education minister Dada Bhuse. Later, Maharashtra police registered a case against the CJP convenor and others for allegedly entering a government school without permission, disrupting official work and threatening teachers.The state governments cited rules to browbeat the CJP teams away from its schools. But at the same time, they were forced to act to nullify the impact of the CJP campaign. So, while some states announced new measures to improve the condition of schools, others increased the pace of work already underway to ensure that results were seen on the ground quickly.The CJP was quick to claim credit for govt actions and basked in glory.“The impact we’ve been able to make with such a small team in such a short span of time is just unreal. Multiple state governments have had to bow down. Authorities had to listen to Gen Z and Gen Alpha kids and give them their due,” it said in a post on X.“But this does not end here. We need to keep going until even the remotest regions of the nation, even the most deprived communities, have access to the highest standard of educational facilities. They may use force, they may file cases, they may do whatever they can to crush this, but we will remain committed to the same demand,” the post read.While it can be debated whether or not the CJP campaign forced the governments into action, what can be said with certainty is that the CJP has managed to do what many political parties could not - inspire the youth to come to the streets and seek accountability from power.The two CJP campaigns also point to an interesting shift - which should be a learning lesson, especially for parties in the opposition space. We have seen the opposition parties raise the pitch against government on issues like caste and religion as these have greater potential for voter mobilisation. Rarely do we see campaigns by the opposition parties centred around health or education reforms. But that seems to have changed.The Congress has taken a cue and is trying to stay focused on students’ connect and raise issues that concern the youth. In Rajasthan, the state Congress unit is also on the streets to highlight gaps in state government school infrastructure.And it’s not just the opposition that is course-correcting; the ruling BJP has also drawn a roadmap to engage with the youth and understand their concerns. In the middle of the Gen Z protest, Prime Minister Narendra Modi debuted on Instagram and tried to communicate directly with the youth who were on the streets. The BJP has in fact formed a dedicated team to spearhead its Gen Z outreach. The team includes BJP chief Nitin Nabin, national general secretaries Smriti Irani and Vinod Tawde, Gujarat minister Harsh Sanghavi, Chhattisgarh minister OP Choudhary, along with several other leaders.Clearly, the CJP has managed to change the political discourse and has put the focus on the youth as potential game-changers in electoral politics. As we gear up for the next rounds of assembly elections in the run-up to the 2029 Lok Sabha challenge, we may see youth outreach taking centre stage like never before.
Article Summary: The Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) “School Thik Karo’ campaign has put the spotlight on the sorry condition of government schools in many states. Gen Z showed the way from Jantar Mantar when they forced the NDA government to make Dharmendra Pradhan resign over NEET paper leaks.

Article Title: In 1978, Richard Branson bought a bare 74-acre Caribbean island for $180,000; it now shelters more than 140 animal species, including breeding lemurs and giant tortoises
Article Text:
An aerial view of Necker Island in the British Virgin Islands, a private island in the Caribbean. Credits - Wikimedia Commons

A reluctant purchase becomes a passion

Building a home for species with nowhere else to go

The Great House on Necker Island, built after Hurricane Irene. Credits - Wikipedia

A sanctuary that sustains itself

In 1978, Richard Branson, then 28, paid $180,000 for a small, uninhabited island in the British Virgin Islands. Necker Island had no fresh water source, no buildings and barely any vegetation beyond scrub and cactus. Nearly fifty years after the purchase, and roughly four decades since the resort itself was completed, that same 74-acre island supports a working conservation programme that shelters well over 140 species, several of which now breed there naturally, including lemurs from Madagascar and giant tortoises from the Seychelles.Branson has told the story of the purchase many times over the years, and the details rarely change. According to an account he has given describing the negotiation, he first visited the British Virgin Islands on a trip meant to impress a woman he was pursuing at the time, having been offered a free look at the islands by a realtor who did not realise how little money Branson actually had. The asking price for Necker was around six million dollars, far beyond what he could afford at the time, running an eight-year-old record label, so Branson made an opening offer of just $100,000.The seller turned him down at first but came back a year later, still unable to find a buyer, and eventually accepted a revised offer of $180,000. At that point he owned essentially raw land, with no infrastructure, and the sale came with a condition that he build a resort on the site within four years. Turning that bare ground into something worth visiting took nearly a decade and set the pattern for what followed: a slow, deliberate transformation rather than a quick development.The wildlife did not arrive all at once, and it was introduced deliberately. Over the decades since the resort was completed, Branson and his team have deliberately introduced species that were struggling in their native ranges, choosing Necker specifically because its isolation from the mainland makes it easier to protect animals from predators and disease, even though the island itself operates as a small, tightly controlled private resort where guest access to the animals is limited and managed by the conservation team. As Branson explains in a PBS documentary filmed on the island, lemurs have become one of what he calls the island's flagship conservation species, brought in after habitat loss in Madagascar left many of their relatives fighting for survival at home. Giant tortoises, native to the Aldabra atoll in the Seychelles, followed a similar path, arriving as part of a breeding programme rather than as a decorative addition to the grounds. Flamingos, macaws, iguanas and a rotating cast of other species have joined them, each one added with the specific aim of giving vulnerable animals a secure place to establish new populations. That patient approach appears to be paying off in the way conservationists actually measure success, through births rather than just headcounts.Today, the tortoises in particular have reached a milestone that is rare in captive conservation work, breeding naturally on the island rather than relying on animals shipped in from elsewhere to maintain their numbers. The breeding success became especially significant in 2021, when the island recorded its first Aldabra giant tortoise hatchlings. The young animals were discovered soon after emerging from their nests and were monitored by the island's conservation team to make sure they remained healthy. The event showed that the tortoises were not simply surviving in an introduced population but were completing an important part of their life cycle on Necker itself. The island's wildlife programme has followed a similar approach with other species, creating conditions in which animals can establish themselves rather than simply being displayed for visitors. Virgin Limited Edition now describes Necker as a natural breeding ground for several rare species, including Madagascan lemurs, giant tortoises, rock lizards and flamingos.A dedicated wildlife team now manages the island's animal population full time, treating Necker less like a private garden and more like a functioning sanctuary with its own breeding programmes and veterinary oversight. Branson himself has framed it in exactly those terms in his own public comments, describing a personal commitment to protecting disappearing species that has clearly outlasted his initial reasons for buying the place at all. Necker Island remains one of a small number of personal purchases from that era that developed decades later into an active conservation programme.
Article Summary: Richard Branson bought Necker Island in 1978 for just $180,000. The 74-acre island now supports a working conservation programme. It shelters well over 140 species, including lemurs from Madagascar and giant tortoises from the Seychelles. A dedicated wildlife team manages the island's population full time.

Article Title: Alaska used rotenone to eliminate invasive pike from an entire lake; the pike vanished, and 6,836 Arctic char were later stocked to rebuild the native fishery
Article Text:
Representative image

Why northern pike are a problem in Alaska

Rotenone: a targeted, temporary reset

Alaska eliminates invasive pike and restocks lake with 6,836 Arctic char

Stormy Lake: a case study in eradication and recovery

Other lakes, similar stories

Why Arctic char matter

Balancing restoration with public concern

A tool, not a silver bullet

In a remote corner of Southcentral Alaska, state biologists carried out a dramatic restoration: they treated an entire lake with rotenone, a plant-derived piscicide, to wipe out an invasive population of northern pike. After the treatment, post-surveys confirmed the pike were gone. The next step was rebuilding what had been lost. In June 2013, the Alaska Department of Fish and Game (ADF&G) stocked 6,836 hatchery-reared Arctic char fingerlings into the now pike-free lake, jump-starting the recovery of a native fishery that had been pushed out by the predator. This account draws on ADF&G’s technical reports and project summaries documenting the rotenone treatment and restocking. Read on to know more:Northern pike are not native to most of Southcentral Alaska. They were illegally introduced into several lakes in the mid-20th century and have since spread through connected waterways, especially as warming temperatures and changing hydrology make it easier for them to move and survive. As apex predators, pike eat large quantities of native fish, including salmon, trout, grayling and char. In some lakes, they have all but replaced native sport fish, collapsing local angling opportunities and altering food webs.ADF&G describes pike as a major threat to endemic fish populations and has pursued a mix of suppression and eradication strategies depending on the waterbody. In isolated lakes where pike can be completely removed, the agency has turned to rotenone as the most practical and efficient tool.Rotenone is a naturally occurring compound derived from certain tropical plants. It has been used for decades in fisheries management to remove unwanted fish from lakes and streams. When applied at carefully calculated concentrations, it blocks oxygen uptake in fish gills, killing fish while leaving most other aquatic organisms unaffected. The chemical breaks down relatively quickly in sunlight and warm water; in many Alaskan projects, detectable levels drop to near zero within weeks to months.There are only two proven methods to eradicate invasive fish from lakes: completely draining the waterbody or using a piscicide like rotenone. For most lakes, draining is not feasible, making rotenone the default option for full eradication. Before treatment, ADF&G typically relocates any desirable native fish, such as salmon or trout, to safe holding areas or other lakes, then treats the target lake and its outlet streams to ensure no pike survive.Stormy Lake, near Anchorage, is one of the clearest examples of this approach. In fall 2012, ADF&G treated Stormy Lake and its outlet creek with liquid rotenone to eradicate an established northern pike population. Post-treatment evaluations—including netting and electrofishing surveys, found no surviving pike, confirming the treatment’s success.Once the rotenone had fully degraded (by late January 2013, about four months after application), the agency began restocking. Native fish that had been held in offsite net pens were reintroduced in March 2013, and on June 17, 2013, ADF&G stocked 6,836 hatchery-reared Arctic char fingerlings into Stormy Lake. These char were of mixed Stormy Lake and Dolly Varden Lake parentage, helping to re-establish a robust, genetically diverse population.The project’s final report, published in ADF&G’s Sport Fish Research series, describes the effort as a successful model for eradicating invasive pike and restoring native fisheries.Stormy Lake is not unique. ADF&G has used rotenone to remove pike from multiple lakes in the Anchorage and Mat-Su areas, including Sand Lake, Anderson Lake and Kings Lake. In each case, the sequence is similar: treat the lake, confirm pike are gone, then restock with native species such as rainbow trout, Arctic char and grayling.For example, after rotenone treatments in 2020, Anderson and Kings lakes were declared pike-free and added to the Northern Cook Inlet stocking program in 2021. Both lakes were restocked with rainbow trout, restoring sport fisheries that had been lost to pike predation. In Anchorage, pike have been eradicated from all but one of five lakes where they were confirmed, with Lower Fire Lake remaining a management challenge.Arctic char are a prized native species in Alaska, valued both ecologically and by anglers. They thrive in cold, clear lakes and are an important part of the natural food web. In lakes where pike have been removed, char are often a key restocking target because they can grow to good size, support recreational fishing and help re-establish a more natural predator–prey balance.In Stormy Lake, the 6,836 char stocked in 2013 were intended to re-create a self-sustaining population that could eventually support a catch-and-release or limited-harvest fishery. Monitoring in subsequent years showed that char, along with other restocked natives, were surviving and growing, indicating the lake was returning to a healthier, pre-pike state.The use of rotenone is not without controversy. Killing all fish in a lake, even temporarily, can be unsettling for nearby residents and anglers. ADF&G addresses these concerns through public meetings, environmental assessments and detailed explanations of why the treatment is necessary and how risks are managed.Agency biologists say allowing pike to remain in the lakes can pose a greater threat to native biodiversity and long-term fishing opportunities. In lakes where pike have become established, native fish may not recover without removing the invasive population completely. When used correctly, rotenone can help achieve this reset, allowing fisheries to be rebuilt with native species.While rotenone has proven effective in isolated lakes, it is not a solution for every pike-infested waterbody. In large, connected systems like much of the Mat-Su Valley, complete eradication is currently impossible because pike can simply move back in from untreated areas. There, ADF&G focuses on suppression, using gillnets, targeted rotenone applications in key tributaries, and liberal harvest rules to keep pike numbers down in priority fisheries.Projects like Stormy Lake show where eradication is still feasible: in relatively closed basins where pike can be fully removed and native fish reintroduced. For those lakes, the combination of rotenone treatment and strategic stocking—like the 6,836 Arctic char released in 2013, offers a path back to a more natural, resilient fishery. For Alaska’s fisheries managers, such projects demonstrate that invasive predators can sometimes be removed and native fish populations rebuilt when the conditions are right. Limited information on Apple CEO John Ternus’ LinkedIn profile

John Ternus recently joined Twitter

Apple’s new CEO John Ternus may have just told millions of professionals around the world that LinkedIn is 'not important' when you are trying to reach the top of the tech industry. John Ternus became Apple CEO on September 1 after more than 25 years at the company, but his LinkedIn profile still does not list him as CEO. It also leaves out much of his career at Apple, including his involvement with major products such as the Apple Watch and AirPods.For someone who has risen to lead one of the world’s biggest technology companies, his limited LinkedIn presence is notable.John Ternus’ LinkedIn page contains only a small amount of information about his professional career. Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture

A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
