Article Title: Niece sent aunt to Delhi fair, then had 60-year-old smothered to death for his Rs 80L gold, but gang couldn't find it
Article Text:
A niece orchestrated her uncle's murder for financial gain.





NEW DELHI: Rakesh Khanna, a 60-year-old man, believed that the money he had got from a real estate deal would secure his twilight years. It instead snuffed out his life. A relative got wind of it and hatched a plot to rob him.What looked like a murder-and-robbery plot soon turned out to be one of greed and betrayal with his wife’s niece, Simran Taneja, emerging as the mastermind behind his killing on Tuesday.Khanna, a resident of Rohini Sector 3, had recently sold a flat for Rs 80 lakh and converted the cash into gold. Armed with intimate knowledge of the family’s routine, Simran, a 23-year-old primary school teacher, allegedly hatched the plot to rob Khanna with her gym-owner boyfriend, Himanshu, trainer Chirag , 22, and Paras,19, a Class XII student previously involved in a case in Mukherjee Nagar.The group did a recce of the premises on Aug 30. On Tuesday afternoon, they struck. Knowing that the gold and money were kept in the house, Simran persuaded her aunt, Khanna’s wife, and other relatives to visit a local fair. This ensured that Khanna, a heart patient, would be alone at home.Simran had procured a duplicate key to the apartment’s central lock. She and Himanshu took positions outside the building around 7.30 pm to keep a watch while the two others entered the house.Chirag and Paras crept up the dimly lit stairs in the house. Khanna stood no chance against the sudden, overwhelming violence of the younger men. They smothered the 60-year-old man to death before he could raise an alarm.Leaving Khanna lifeless on the floor, the two men ransacked the house, tearing through cupboards and drawers in a desperate hunt for the gold. But Khanna had been cautious. Despite their efforts, the two managed to take away only about Rs 1.5 lakh in cash and some gold jewellery.Most of the gold remained safely concealed in the house with even Khanna’s family unsure where he had hidden it.When Khanna’s wife returned from the fair, she stepped into a ransacked home with her husband lying motionless on the floor. She dialled the cops at 8.15 pm to report what looked like a break-in. Khanna was rushed to Jaipur Golden Hospital where he was declared dead.Special CP (law and order) Devesh Chandra Shrivastava formed a 12-member team, led by joint commissioner Vijay Singh and DCP Shashank Jaiswal, to investigate the case. When cops and a forensic team got down to their job, the plot began to unravel quickly. The police stumbled upon breadcrumbs left behind by the suspects, and their mobile phone locations also gave them away. Studying CCTV footage from the area, the cops also noticed some suspicious movement a few days before the murder.Simran was found to be loitering near the house after the murder, trying to monitor the police response. When questioned about her movements on Aug 30, she gave conflicting answers, prompting the police to analyse her mobile call records and WhatsApp details.It took just three hours to crack the case. Three of the accused — Simran, Chirag and Paras — were caught. Himanshu is on the run.The police have also recovered Rs 70,000 of the stolen money and gold jewellery. A case was registered at South Rohini police station, and the accused produced in court and taken on remand.
Article Summary: Rakesh Khanna, a 60-year-old man, believed that the money he had got from a real estate deal would secure his twilight years. His wife’s niece, Simran Taneja, emerged as the mastermind behind his killing on Tuesday.

Article Title: No cement: KEM tries new-age knee implant for first time in Mumbai
Article Text:
Unlike conventional knee replacements, which use bone cement to fix the implant, cementless implants have a porous surface that allows the patient’s bone to grow into and secure the implant

Mumbai:





Times News NetworkWhen 70-year-old Prakash Waigankar was told he needed a total knee replacement, he sought opinions from several doctors. While some recommended surgery, others advised him to wait.The Goregaon resident then turned to KEM Hospital in Parel, an institution he had known since childhood. Doctors advised surgery but offered him a newer option: a cementless knee implant, which they said was being performed for the first time in Mumbai.On Aug 24, Waigankar underwent a left total knee replacement using the customised implant.“My left knee was bent, but now it is straight after the surgery. The pain is so much less than before,” he said.Unlike conventional knee replacements, which use bone cement to fix the implant, cementless implants have a porous surface that allows the patient’s bone to grow into and secure the implant. Prof Dr S Mohanty of KEM’s orthopaedic department, who performed the surgery, said the technique could become increasingly relevant as younger and more active patients undergo knee replacements.“Cement can eventually come loose. The cementless implant has a porous surface that allows bone to grow into it, making the fixation firmer.This is designed for the long term,” he said.Cemented fixation remains the standard for knee replacement, but concerns over loosening have fuelled interest in cementless implants, particularly for younger patients, according to a 2021 review in the Indian Journal of Orthopaedics by New York-based Dr Amar S Ranawat.Dr Mohanty said cementless hip replacements had been used for much longer, while the technology for knees was relatively newer. Cost had been a barrier, but Indian-made implants could make the procedure more affordable, he said.At KEM, the medical team led by Dr Mohanty and dean Dr Harish Pathak worked for a week to secure the first-in-Mumbai achievement; one of the first tasks was to order the customised implant for Waigankar from the Indian company, which arrived in four to five days. “There is one instance of cementless knee replacement being used in Delhi, after that it is Waigankar’s surgery,” said the doctors.For Waigankar, the benefit was immediate and tangible: after living with a bent and painful knee, he can now stand straighter. “I am happy that I decided to come to KEM,” he said.
Article Summary: Unlike conventional knee replacements, which use bone cement to fix the implant, cementless implants have a porous surface that allows the patient’s bone to grow into and secure the implant. Prakash Waigankar, 70, underwent a left total knee replacement using the customised implant.

Article Title: 1st girl child in 4 generations: Beed family stages grand celebration to mark birth of newborn
Article Text:
A family celebrated the birth of a girl child after a four-generation wait





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: The joy of the Dahiphale family from Parli in Maharashtra's Beed district, around 210km from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, knew no bounds as a girl child was born into their family after a wait of four generations.The family welcomed the newborn and her mother by arranging a special procession featuring a decorated chariot on August 29.The video of the procession has gone viral and has drawn praise, especially against the backdrop of Beed having recently gained a notorious reputation for multiple cases of female foeticide Grandfather Limbaji Dahiphale, who is serving as a school principal, said the family had been yearning for a girl child."No girl child had been born in our lineage for almost four generations. I have two sons and my elder son has one son. We are glad that God has now blessed my younger son with a girl child," he said.Born on August 24, the girl has been named Gargi, after the sage and philosopher from the Vedic period.On her discharge from the hospital, Gargi and her mother were brought home in a beautifully decorated chariot accompanied by the beats of dhol-tasha, cymbals, and folk dance.Family members, relatives, and villagers showered flowers and danced as the chariot made its way home, turning the homecoming into a grand spectacle.The girl's father, Hrishikesh, who is a pharmacist by profession, said it is a great fortune to have a daughter in the family."For so many years, we missed a girl child in our family, especially on occasions like Raksha Bandhan and Bhau Beej. I personally believe that daughters are more caring and loving towards their father compared to sons," he said.The family said the decision to hold a grand celebration for the newborn's homecoming was taken at the hospital itself.President of Parli Vaijnath Municipal Council, Padmashri Dharmadhikari said the birth of Gargi on the sacred land of Parli Vaijnath, one of the 12 Jyotirlinga sites, after wait of four generations by the family is a moment of immense joy."Dahiphale family is an example for the entire society as their gesture overcomes traditional gender biases," she said
Article Summary: The Dahiphale family from Parli in Maharashtra's Beed district celebrated the birth of a girl child after a four-generation wait. Article Title: Maharashtra horror: Teen murdered, body dumped near Mini Seashore
Article Text:
A 19-year-old man was found murdered near a public garden in Vashi





NAVI MUMBAI: A 19-year-old boy was murdered and his body was dumped on the pavement near a public garden along Mini Seashore Road in Sector 10A, Vashi, early on Saturday morning. The Vashi police have registered a murder case against unidentified accused.Shashikant Chandekar, senior inspector of Vashi police station, said, "The murder victim was identified as Sujan Kumar Mahato, a resident of Sector 19, Koparkhairane. A passing pedestrian spotted him lying unconscious in a pool of blood on the pavement around 4am. The pedestrian alerted Vashi police station, and our police team reached the spot and took the teenager to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead due to severe blood loss from grievous injuries to his head and wrist after being assaulted with some sharp lethal weapon. The victim Mahato hails from Bihar and resided with his father, who is an auto-rickshaw driver, his mother and two minor siblings. He worked at a roadside Chinese food stall in Koparkhairane and used to drive his father's auto-rickshaw during the night."Inspector Chandekar added, "Mahato had left home on Friday around 9pm, telling his mother that he was going to work at the Chinese food stall and was taking his father's auto-rickshaw to ferry passengers throughout the night.After his body was found early on Saturday morning, his family was informed. His father's auto-rickshaw was not found at the crime scene. Hence, it is suspected that after fatally assaulting Mahato, the assailant took away the auto-rickshaw, which is being traced by scanning CCTV footage along the route from Koparkhairane to Vashi."As there is no CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we are scanning CCTV footage from roads leading to the crime spot where Mahato's body was dumped to zero in on the suspect. Mahato might have been fatally assaulted at the spot, or he might have been assaulted at another location and his body brought in a vehicle and dumped near Mini Seashore. Accordingly, using technical expertise, efforts are being made to detect the murder case. Meanwhile, Mahato's kin and friends are being questioned to get some lead on the unidentified accused."

Article Title: Navi Mumbai road rage: Ola driver attacked with stick, dragged 2km on car bonnet
Article Text:
The incident occured on the stretch of Sarsole village road in sector 20 near Nerul pond on Aug 15 around 9.35pm.





NAVI MUMBAI: In a road rage incident in Nerul after an argument between the drivers of an Ola cab and a Swift car as the latter claimed that the Ola cab driver had dangerously cut his way while overtaking on the internal road in Nerul on August 15 night, the Swift car driver assaulted the cab driver by punching on his nose and hitting on the head with a bamboo stick causing him severe injuries.As the cab driver bled profusely and attempted to stop the car driver from getting away till the cops arrived, by lying on the car's bonnet, the car driver drove with the cab driver on the bonnet for about 2 kms.The cab driver while recording the incident on his mobile in one hand and firmly holding the bonnet by other hand, shouted for help from passing motorists, while dangling dangerously and requesting the car driver to stop by yelling that he could fall and get killed.As the car slowed down after some distance, the cab driver jumped off the bonnet after which the car driver sped away leaving the cab driver injured on the road.The incident occured on the stretch in sector 20 near Nerul pond on August 15 around 9.35pm.Ajay Kamble, senior inspector of Nerul said, "As per the complaint by the injured cab driver identified as Pradeepkumar Pandey, 27, a resident of Naigaon (E), an FIR was registered at Nerul police station against the unidentified accused car driver, who is absconding.From the Swift car's registration number provided by the complainant, the accused driver was identified as Lalit Arjun Patil, a resident of Juinagar. ""We have invoked relevant BNS sections for the offences of voluntarily causing hurt/ grievous hurt using dangerous weapons or means, voluntarily causing simple hurt, rash or negligent driving on a public way in a manner that endangers human life or is likely to cause hurt or injury to any person and causing simple hurt to any person through a rash or negligent act that endangers human life or personal safety," inspector Kamble added.As per the FIR, on August 15 at 8.18pm, the complainant Pandey had picked up two women passengers from Andheri and dropped them at Seawoods Grand Central mall in Nerul at around 9.30pm.Thereafter, he headed towards Sarsole to attend birthday party of his cousin Nitin Pandey's brother-in-law Rahul Chaubey.Around 9.35pm, when he reached near Nerul pond in sector 20, suddenly a Swift car driver was repeatedly honking. Hence, he changed the lane and gave him way to go ahead.But, the car driver waylaid him and alighting from his car claimed that he had dangerously cut his way while overtaking and punched on his nose, while hurling expletives.As the complainant tried to convince him and told not to give bad words, the car driver went to his vehicle and taking out a bamboo stick, hit on his head causing severe bleeding.As the assailant sat in his car, the complainant tried to stop him, but he started his car. Hence, the complainant lied on the car's bonnet to prevent him from escaping till the cops arrived.The assailant drove with the complainant on the bonnet for about 2kms, reluctant to stop the car.After some distance, as the car slowed down, he jumped off the bonnet and the assailant sped away.The complainant returned to his cab and called his cousin Dipanshu Pandey, who took him to NMMC's Meenatai Thackeray hospital, Nerul.The doctors gave him first aid and for further treatment referred him to NMMC hospital in Vashi, where he was administered sutures to head injury, followed by CT scan.Thereafter, he lodged a police complaint.
Article Summary: The incident occured on the stretch of Sarsole village road in sector 20 near Nerul pond on Aug 15 around 9.35pm. Article Title: Man falls from 7th floor, iron rod pierces intestine and bone; walks again
Article Text:
Kumar had an emergency surgery in Kalyan to remove rod





KALYAN: When Cheena Kumar, 33, fell from the 7th floor at a construction site in Ambernath on July 28, an iron reinforcement rod pierced his body, passing through his pelvis and lower abdomen before protruding through his abdomen.Against odds, Kumar survived the fall, the horrific injury and massive blood loss. He is now back with his family in Uttar Pradesh and is able to walk with support.“I never thought I would survive,” said Kumar, recalli­ng the moments before he lo­st consciousness. A farmer fr­om Siddharth Nagar distr­i­ct,UP, Kumar had moved to Ambernath just six months earlier to take up his first job outside agriculture.After his fall, he was rushed to Fortis Hospital, Kal­yan, where doctors perform­ed an emergency surgery as his blood pressure was critically low.He is the first member of his family to leave farming for construction work. His wife, two children, parents and brother continue to live in the village.The fall left him with a severe open fracture of his left thigh bone, extensive soft-tissue injuries and haemorrhagic shock. About 20-25cm of the rod remained protruding from his body.He was rushed to Fortis Hospital, Kalyan, where scans showed that the rod had pierced his small intestine at several points and passed through the iliac bone.It had narrowly missed the ureter and major blood vessels supplying his left leg.With his blood pressure critically low, doctors proceeded with emergency surgery after reviewing the scan images rather than waiting for the formal CT report. The rod was removed, the intestinal injuries were repaired, and the contaminated wounds were cleaned.Kumar recovered without developing an infection and was discharged after about a week.He has since returned to Uttar Pradesh to be with his family. Although he still needs support to walk, he says he is recovering well with their help.“I never thought I would survive, and today I am able to walk with support. I cannot thank the doctors enough for bringing me back on my feet,” he said, still unable to decide if he will return to Mumbai.
Article Summary: Cheena Kumar, 33, fell from the 7th floor at a construction site in Ambernath. Iron reinforcement rod pierced his body, passing through his pelvis and lower abdomen before protruding through his abdomen. Kumar survived the fall, the horrific injury and massive blood loss and is now back with his family in Uttar Pradesh.

PUNE: A 65-year-old farmer and his ailing wife were allegedly abused and beaten with wooden sticks by their two sons in Maharashtra's Pune district following a dispute over the sale of land owned by the woman.The incident took place on August 30 in Indapur when the elderly couple had stepped out for an evening walk, police said.According to police, the couple's two sons arrived at the spot in a car and allegedly began abusing their parents over the sale of a parcel of land belonging to their mother. The argument soon turned violent, with the two men allegedly attacking the couple with wooden sticks.The farmer suffered injuries to his face, back, thighs and left shoulder, while his wife was injured on her right wrist and waist.Police said the accused also allegedly threatened the couple with serious consequences if they did not cancel the land deal.Passersby alerted the police, following which a team rushed to the spot and took the injured couple to a hospital. After receiving preliminary treatment, the farmer approached Indapur police and lodged a complaint against his sons.The two accused have been booked under sections 118 (voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means), 351 (criminal intimidation) and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of peace) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Article Title: Farmer, wife beaten up by sons over land deal in Indapur
Article Text:
Pune:





A 65-year-old farmer from Indapur and his wife were allegedly abused and thrashed with wooden sticks by their two sons over the sale of a parcel of land belonging to their mother on Aug 30 when the couple were taking an evening walk.The farmer suffered injuries to his face, back, thighs and left shoulder, while his wife suffered injuries to her right wrist and waist. The farmer later approached Indapur police and lodged a complaint. The farmer’s sons have been charged under sections 118 (voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means), 351 (criminal intimidation) and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).An officer from the Indapur police said the farmer had taken his ailing wife out for a walk on Aug 30. Their two sons reached the spot in a car and started abusing them over the sale of a parcel of land belonging to their mother. “The duo thrashed their parents with wooden sticks. They threatened them with dire consequences if they did not cancel the deal,” the officer said.The officer said some passersby alerted the police. “Our team took the couple to a hospital. After receiving preliminary treatment, the farmer lodged a complaint against his sons,” he said.

Article Title: Speeding auto knocks youth dead, driver flees
Article Text:
Nagpur:





A 26-year-old man died after a speeding autorickshaw hit him in Pratap Nagar and fled on Tuesday.The deceased, Rishabh Mahindra Shende, was a resident of plot no. 89 behind Panchyashi Mandir in Mata Nagar. The autorickshaw was being driven by Ijaz Khan Pathan (26), a resident of Sakkardara.The complainant, who was present at the spot, rushed Shende to a hospital, where he succumbed during treatment.Pratap Nagar police registered a case against the autorickshaw driver, who is reportedly absconding. Police inspector Pankaj Bodse’s team has launched a search to trace the accused.
